hypothesis: Trading in the direction of the 200-period trend outperforms trading against it.
falsifierStatedBeforeRunning: The with-trend minus against-trend difference must hold the same sign in train, validate AND sealed, instrument agreement must beat a coin flip, and with-trend must itself be positive on sealed data with an interval excluding zero. Being less bad than the opposite is not an edge.
method: Every entry rule, every instrument, hourly bars. Stop 3x ATR, ladder 1.2/2.0/3.5R, cost = spread/stop distance, stop checked before targets, non-overlapping. The ONLY variable is whether the signal direction agrees with price against its 200-period average. One pre-specified comparison, so no multiple-testing correction is owed.
verdict: NOT ESTABLISHED. On the sealed quarter with-trend beat against-trend by 0.0611R at t=2.35, which looks like a result. It is not one. Measured window by window the difference is +0.0522R in training, -0.0767R in validation and +0.0612R sealed. The sign flips, so this is not one mechanism measured three times. In the validation window trading AGAINST the 200-period trend returned 0.0591R at t=2.96 — the opposite of the claim, and more significant than the claim. 11 of 19 instruments agree, p=0.648 against a coin flip. And with-trend itself returns -0.0109R on sealed data with interval [-0.043, 0.0212], so even taken at face value it is not profitable. The 7-of-8 pattern in the 288-combination search was selection, not a mechanism: those combinations reached the sealed set by performing well in training and validation, which is the very thing the family test then read back off them.
